problem: SFT policies for VLN-CE suffer compounding errors and cannot recover from OOD states, while GRPO-style RFT is bottlenecked by sparse binary outcome rewards. Credit is not assigned to individual steps, and all-failure batches yield zero relative advantage (gradient collapse).
motivation: About 73% of failed episodes execute the initial sub-instructions correctly, so failed rollouts hold useful dense supervision that standard RL discards. Training domain-specific process reward models is costly and prone to reward hacking, so a zero-shot way to mine step-level signals from failures is desirable.
key_idea: Use a zero-shot perception auditor (instruction landmarks + CLIP/GroundingDINO/SAM3) to give each trajectory a soft process score and a hard-mask divergence point, then route GRPO groups to Repair Resampling (mixed groups) or All-Failure Rescue (null groups) with step-level alignment and contrastive-correction losses.
insight: Dense supervision recovered from failures is what lifts performance: adding the soft score, then All-Failure Rescue, then Repair Resampling improves RxR-CE SR from 49.9 (plain GRPO) to 51.8, 56.4 and 60.3, and the SR curves show plain GRPO plateauing while the full method keeps improving. The auditor's perception cascade matters (CLIP only 57.6 SR, +GroundingDINO 59.2, +SAM3 60.3 on R2R-CE). The step-level losses and conservative advantage scaling each add 1-3 points, showing that noisy visual process estimates must be handled cautiously.
method: PGSA auditor: a frozen Qwen3-0.6B parses the instruction into landmarks; per step, the soft score S_t fuses global CLIP similarity, GroundingDINO detection confidence and SAM3-masked CLIP similarity (w=0.3/0.3/0.4). The trajectory process score R_proc is the length-normalised ReLU(S_t - tau_s) average.

Structural hard mask: M_t = 1[S_t > tau_h]; the active landmark advances after c=2 consecutive hard matches; the divergence point t_div is the first step with M_t=0, splitting a valid prefix from the divergent suffix.

Repair Resampling (mixed group): for failures with t_div/T > eta=0.5, truncate at t_div and resample suffixes up to N_rep=3 times; successful repaired trajectories are added with a suffix behavior-cloning loss (lambda_rep).

All-Failure Rescue (null group): pick the highest-R_proc failure as pseudo-anchor, mine top-m hard negatives by an LCS prefix-similarity plus score-gap criterion, and form a reflection sub-group with process-score advantages normalised inside it.
Conservative advantages: margin-based rescue shrinks advantages by kappa=0.5 when the anchor-vs-negatives margin is below delta=0.1; negative-only scaling multiplies negative advantages by s=0.5.

Step-level constraints on the anchor only: L_align is behavior cloning on the valid prefix; L_corr is an InfoNCE-style contrastive loss at t_div pulling the hidden state toward a teacher action a+ (from the simulator shortest path) and away from the erroneous action a-.
Training pipeline: LLaVA-Video-8B initialised policy, SFT (2 epochs, lr 1e-5), then RFT with K=8 rollouts, lr 1e-6, KL beta 0.04.

setting.backbone: LLaVA-Video-8B Video-LLM policy (SFT then RFT); frozen Qwen3-0.6B, GroundingDINO, SAM3 and CLIP used only in the training-time auditor
setting.training_data: R2R-CE and RxR-CE training data for SFT and RFT; the dagger variant adds extra data (ScaleVLN, following StreamVLN) beyond R2R-CE/RxR-CE
setting.observation: monocular egocentric RGB with video history (no depth, odometry or panorama)
setting.action_space: low-level discrete: TURN LEFT/RIGHT 15°, MOVE FORWARD 25 cm, STOP
setting.privileged: none at test time; training uses simulator shortest-path teacher action at the divergence point and environment success as the outcome reward

numbers_note: The text says SACA† reaches 62.7% SR on R2R-CE, which conflicts with the 64.7 printed in Table 1; the table value is used. The text also says 3.3% gain over ETPNav on R2R SR, which is inconsistent with the table (60.3 vs 57.0 is consistent, fine).
results: SACA reaches 60.3 SR / 55.1 SPL on R2R-CE val-unseen and 60.3 SR / 49.8 SPL on RxR-CE with single RGB and no extra data, beating StreamVLN (52.8/47.2 and 48.6/42.5). With extra data it gets 64.7 SR on R2R-CE and 62.1 SR on RxR-CE, beating StreamVLN† (56.9 and 52.9), and it also surpasses panoramic+depth ETPNav (57.0 / 54.7 SR).
limitations: Reward quality depends on the frozen perception stack (GroundingDINO, SAM3, CLIP) and on a tiny LLM's landmark parsing, so it may be noisy; the paper needs conservative scaling to cope.
Training is expensive (about 36 h for SFT plus 24 h per RFT epoch on 8 A6000 GPUs) and the method needs simulator shortest-path teacher actions and landmark-based instructions.
Evaluated only in the Habitat simulator on R2R-CE and RxR-CE, with no real-robot tests; extra-data comparisons are not fully controlled.
